notes: Both stories were deferred from earlier sprints. Decals come from the S109 FEAT-PROCEDURAL-TEXTURING proposal; recipe sync is the Option B path called out in docs/research/kaboom-multiplayer-plan.md §2.

stories.title: Procedural texturing Layer 2 — body decals (chestEmblem / helmetStripe / kneePad) via vertex-color masks
stories.summary:
Three starter decals applied as vertex-colour overrides at specific anchor faces on specific part-meshes. NO shader changes — the decal is painted directly onto the vertex colour buffer in the per-part builder, so the existing vertexColors=true MeshStandardMaterial picks it up for free.

- chestEmblem: small square on the FRONT face of the torso (Z extreme, mid-Y, mid-X band). Painted with palette.accent.
- helmetStripe: horizontal band across the top half of the head. Painted with palette.accent.
- kneePad: small square on the FRONT face of each lowerLeg's upper third. Painted with palette.handFoot (or palette.upperLeg darker variant for now — palette doesn't expose handFoot yet).

Recipe field: `texturing.decals: ('chestEmblem'|'helmetStripe'|'kneePad')[]` — 0..3, picked deterministically from seed when unspecified. Each part-builder reads the array + paints the appropriate vertices when the decal applies to that part.

Approach: instead of shader-side emissive masks (proposal's original direction), paint the decal vertices with the decal colour directly. To get crisp edges, bump the relevant face's subdivisions where needed (torso front face widthSegments / depthSegments, head top face).

Determinism: same seed + same texturing block → bit-identical vertex-colour buffer. Test with multiple seeds.
verification: acceptance: Procedural texturing Layer 2 (body decals) shipped. Recipe gains optional texturing.decals: ('chestEmblem'|'helmetStripe'|'kneePad')[] (0..3, deterministic order, unique items). Pure vertex-colour overrides on top of the S109 panel-seams pass — no shader change. Torso BoxGeometry bumped to (2,2,2) segments (54 verts) so the FRONT face has a 3x3 grid where chestEmblem lands crisply. Each decal scoped to its anchor part: chestEmblem → torso FRONT face mid-band, helmetStripe → head upper-half, kneePad → lowerLeg upper-third front strip. Bench UI gains 3 decal-toggle checkboxes. Recipe codec round-trips the decals array.
examples/procbomber-bench/src/generators/bomber-parts.ts: DECAL_KINDS / DecalKind types, applyDecals helper, partName + palette threaded through applyTexturing, torso BoxGeometry 2x2x2
examples/procbomber-bench/src/character-recipe.ts: decals in BomberTexturing, resolveTexturing default = [], validator accepts the array + uniqueItems
examples/procbomber-bench/src/bench-state.ts + bench-ui.ts + recipe-url.ts: state.decals + texturingOf + UI checkboxes + recipe sync
+7 unit tests covering each decal's predicate, deterministic output, multi-decal independence, decal scoped to right part
Existing torso vert-count tests updated 32→54 for the (2,2,2) segments change. No behavioural regression — every other part stays at 32.

stories.title: Multiplayer recipe sync — remote bombers use the actual player's recipe (Option B)
stories.summary:
S109's connect-and-spectate kickoff renders remote bombers from a fallback seed (resolveRecipeFromSeed('remote.' + playerId)). The plan (docs/research/kaboom-multiplayer-plan.md §2 Option B) is to carry the local player's resolved recipe in the snapshot so the OTHER tab renders the bomber that's actually walking around.

Approach: the server is a Transform-only world (`examples/backends/node-world-server`). It doesn't track CharacterRecipe. Two reasonable paths:

  (a) Client-side gossip: each client posts its recipe via a new probe message `player.recipe` that the server echoes verbatim in every player.<id> snapshot entity's `CharacterRecipe` component. Adds one schema entry to protocol.schema.json.
  (b) URL-driven: each tab passes its recipe as a `?recipe=<base64>` URL param; the player.join message carries it; server stores per-player and includes in snapshots.

Recommend (b) — simpler, no new message kind, recipe is already URL-encodable via encodeRecipe(). The kaboom-crew bootstrap detects `?recipe=` on the connected path, stamps the recipe on the local bomber AND forwards via player.join.displayName-like channel (extend the player.join payload). Remote-bomber decorator system reads CharacterRecipe from the snapshot entity instead of synthesising from the player id.

Out of scope: server-side validation of the recipe (untrusted clients; treat input as best-effort); recipe edits mid-session.
verification: acceptance: Multiplayer recipe sync (Option B) shipped. Each tab forwards its ?recipe= URL param to the server via player.join.payload.recipe (opaque base64-url-safe blob, 4 KB cap, server treats as untrusted). ServerWorld stores the recipe per player and emits it as a CharacterRecipe component on the player.<id> snapshot entity. The kaboom-crew remote-bomber decorator decodes the recipe via decodeRecipe + resolveRecipeFromSeed(decoded.seed, decoded) and spawns the bomber tree with the actual visual identity, falling back to the S109 seed-from-id path when the snapshot has no CharacterRecipe OR the blob fails to decode. Re-join with a different recipe overwrites; re-join without a recipe keeps the previous one (idempotent join, reconnect-friendly).
schemas/protocol.schema.json: player.join.payload gains optional 'recipe' string (4 KB cap)
examples/backends/node-world-server/src/world.ts: ServerWorld.join(playerId, recipe?) + snapshot() emits CharacterRecipe component
examples/backends/node-world-server/src/transport-ws.ts: extracts recipe from player.join payload + forwards to world.join
src/app.ts + src/main.ts: AppOptions.recipe forwarded from ?recipe= URL param into the WS adapter
examples/kaboom-crew/src/systems/remote-bomber-decorator-system.ts: reads CharacterRecipe from snapshot entity, decodes via decodeRecipe, falls back to seed-from-id on missing or malformed recipe
+5 server-side world tests (recipe carry, multiple players, reconnect overwrite, idempotent re-join) + 3 client-side decorator tests (decode path, S109 fallback, malformed fallback) = +8 unit tests
Full suite 1300/1300 on a clean run.
